concept.name: Volume value area
concept.definition: The value area computed from a volume profile rather than from TPO counts: the contiguous price band around the volume point of control that contains a chosen percentage — conventionally 70% — of the period's total traded volume, bounded by the volume-based VAH and VAL.
concept.intuition: It is the price range where 70% of the actual contracts changed hands, as opposed to the TPO value area's 70% of time.
concept.mechanics: Total volume in the profile is multiplied by the target percentage; starting at the VPOC, rows are added alternately from the side with the larger adjacent volume until the target is reached, and the extreme included rows become VAH and VAL.
concept.formula: Target volume = 0.70 × total profile volume; expand from the VPOC row, always adding the larger of the next row above or below, until the enclosed volume reaches the target
concept.failure_modes: On multi-modal distributions the single contiguous band misrepresents where volume actually sits, and the 70% default is a convention; up/down volume splits on platforms use bar-direction approximations rather than true buy/sell classification.
concept.misconceptions: The volume value area and the TPO value area are not interchangeable — on days with uneven volume across brackets they can differ materially, and mixing references from both muddies the analysis.
concept.example: A session profile totals 1.6M contracts; expanding from the VPOC until 1.12M (70%) are enclosed yields VAH 4,528 and VAL 4,509, inside which the next day's open is read as acceptance.
